_doc: A session on a pinned, public corpus. Everything a skeptic needs to
reproduce or attack this run is in this file: the corpus commit, the exact
edits, the questions, and the expected answers.
locate     'where is X' — a line matcher CAN answer these, and does. We
expect to draw or lose here on speed; that is the honest shape.
relate     'who calls X / what breaks if I change X' — needs a call graph.
Tools without one are marked n/a, never 0.
staleness  asked ONLY after an edit. Two directions per rename:
expect_absent  the OLD name must be gone   (stale index fails)
expect_any     the NEW name must be found  (dead index fails)
This is the check that stops 'incremental in 0ms by doing
nothing' from looking like a win.
GRADING is exact word-boundary match on the tool's own stdout. No LLM, no
rubric. The price of that rigour is that every expectation must be a symbol
that is textually unambiguous, which is why these sets are small and

corpus.name: Newtonsoft.Json
corpus.note: public, pinned by tag; the same corpus the golden judged tier uses

description: Build once, ask, edit, re-index, ask again — 2 rounds.

questions.known_weakness: scores 0.0 in our own judged tier (N01): test files outrank the source method. Kept deliberately — a question set with no losses in it is a sales deck.

questions.why: declared JsonTextReader.cs:1136, called from ParseString (:157->:162) and ParseProperty. A call graph reaches them; a line matcher cannot. Uses the QUALIFIED label because `affected` correctly refuses to guess between ReadStringIntoBuffer / ...Async / FinishReadStringIntoBuffer.
blast radius of a private parser method — any real impact answer names its file or a caller.

edits.why: Word-boundary safe: it does NOT touch FinishReadStringIntoBuffer or ReadStringIntoBufferAsync, which contain the name but not at a boundary. The harness verifies the count and aborts if the corpus drifted from the pin.

probes.why: the renamed-away symbol must no longer be reported; an index that never updated still returns it
the new symbol must be findable; an index that never updated cannot see it

rounds.name: touch a widely-included file (mtime only, content identical)

edits.why: No semantic change. Measures whether a tool does needless work on a stat-level signal — a content-hash tool should be near-free here, an mtime tool re-indexes.
